### 🟡 Off-by-one in array bounds check allows index equal to length

The function contract states it throws RangeError outside the array, but valid nonnegative indices of an array with length n are 0 through n-1. The guard `index > values.length` uses a strict greater-than, so `at(values, values.length)` is treated as in-bounds and returns `undefined` rather than throwing. The check should be `index >= values.length`.

**Evidence:** Guard reads `if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > values.length)`; at index === values.length the expression `index > values.length` is false, so `return values[index]` executes and yields undefined.

**Suggested change:**

Change the comparison to `index >= values.length` so that index equal to the array length throws RangeError.

<sub>correctness · confidence 99%</sub>
